rows.fault_trigger: Flat Backside Foot. Letting the heel of the staggered back foot touch the grass flat, which deadens the leg muscle and creates an immediate delay on the snap.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Position feet strictly shoulder-width apart with a comfortable toe-to-instep stagger, placing the inside foot forward. Shade alignment reference: on outside shade, the corner's inside foot aligns with the receiver's outside foot; on inside shade, the corner's outside foot aligns with the receiver's inside foot.

rows.fault_trigger: "Lifting the Gate" (Lifting or Stepping Forward). Taking a step forward at the snap, which completely destroys the corner's cushion and allows a fast receiver to blow past them instantly.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: At the snap, take a concise 2-to-3 inch step backward without gaining or losing massive ground.

rows.fault_trigger: Dropping the Inside Foot. Stepping backward with the inside foot first, which opens the inside lane completely.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drive off the outside foot at the snap to slide laterally inside if the receiver attempts to cross your face.
Brace the base and push hard off the inside foot at the snap.

rows.fault_trigger: Bailing Too Fast. Flying backward at a full sprint immediately, which completely gives up the intermediate space and opens up easy 10-yard curl, hitch, or out routes.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Push off the front foot directly into a tempo-controlled backward pedal.

rows.fault_trigger: Losing the Sideline Cushion. Pedaling in a straight vertical line and allowing a fast receiver to step on your toes and blow past your outside shoulder.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Begin the deep backpedal with an intentional, subtle drift toward the sideline boundary.

rows.fault_trigger: Losing Pad Level. Rising straight up out of the stance on the first step, which slows down backward velocity.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Push directly off the forward foot to launch straight backward into a high-tempo pedal.

rows.fault_trigger: Sprinting Out Early. Immediately turning and running deep on the snap, which allows the receiver to easily break off an intermediate route into 10-12 yards of completely open space. Also: Flat Feet - standing static at 10 yards and letting a high-speed vertical receiver erase the cushion completely before you start moving.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take a slow, deliberate "read-step" backward (a spatial "tempo pedal") to absorb the receiver's initial release.
Initiate a deep, high-cushion backpedal with a slight outward tracking angle toward the sideline.

rows.fault_trigger: False Stepping Forward. Taking a step forward out of a 10-yard stance, which defeats the entire purpose of playing deep cushion.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Glide dynamically out of the stance using low, sweeping backward steps.
Unweight the stance by loading 60% of the body weight onto the ball of the front foot and 40% on the back foot.

rows.fault_trigger: "Bending at the Waist". Leaning the upper body too far forward over the knees, which shifts weight onto the toes and traps the hips, making it impossible to transition into a clean backpedal.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink the hips smoothly into an athletic quarter-squat, ensuring the chest sits directly over the knees, and knees over the toes.
Keep the spine long and flat to prevent the hips from locking or trapping the cornerback's center of gravity.

rows.fault_trigger: Hands on Knees. Resting hands on the thighs pre-snap, which completely exposes the chest to a wide receiver's immediate release jam.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold the hands loose and highly active strictly at chest height, prepared to punch, steer, or match a sudden release.
Keep the feet wide and actively moving on parallel tracks.
Lock the eyes firmly on the receiver's beltline and hips to read their true center of gravity.
Hold ground and mirror the receiver's lateral movements from a static motor-shuffle.

rows.fault_trigger: Premature Two-Hand Punch. Reaching out with both hands early, which robs the corner of their balance and allows the receiver to easily swipe the arms away.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Withhold the hands until the receiver fully commits to a release lane, then strike.
If the receiver accepts the outside path, immediately transition into a lateral Kick-Slide.

rows.fault_trigger: Biting on Outside Fakes. Opening the inside hip and stepping out toward the sideline on a receiver's outside release fake, completely giving up the inside leverage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish and aggressively maintain an inside-out trailing relationship.
Fire the inside hand directly into the receiver's chest plate to establish physical control.
Steer the receiver forcefully wide toward the sideline boundary, protecting the middle of the field at all costs.

rows.fault_trigger: Allowing a Free Outside Release. Letting the receiver beat you cleanly down the sideline by stepping too narrow or failing to slide wide on the first step.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take a rapid lateral shuffle step to the outside to perfectly cap the receiver's outside track.

rows.fault_trigger: Turning the Hips Early. Turning the entire body to face the sideline on the snap, leaving you exposed to an easy inside cutback.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the chest completely square to the line of scrimmage as the receiver initiates contact.
Fire a violent, aggressive outside-hand jam directly to the receiver's outside shoulder.
Physically cap their vertical path and funnel them strictly inside toward your middle-of-the-field safety help.
Keep the chin strictly tucked with the shoulders leaning slightly forward over the toes.
Execute a subtle drift or weave to the inside during the pedal to maintain inside-out leverage advantage.

rows.fault_trigger: Clicking Heels. Shuffling or pedaling so erratically that the feet click together, leaving the corner off-balance when the receiver breaks vertically.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the backward steps fluid and low to the turf, reaching backward specifically with the toes.
Protect the inside lane while keeping the intermediate cushion intact as the receiver climbs vertically.
Preserve outside leverage to stay on top of any deep sideline route concepts.

rows.fault_trigger: Staring at the QB. Peeking into the backfield early in man coverage, which causes you to completely miss the receiver's break point.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep eyes glued exclusively to the receiver's lower abdomen to track speed and depth metrics.
Maintain the outside bias strictly to force all intermediate tracks inside.
Prime the hips to execute a sudden "Kick-Turn" or hip-flip to the outside the moment the vertical cushion is threatened.
Execute a highly disciplined, completely vertical neutral backpedal to match the receiver's speed step-for-step.
Strictly maintain a 3-to-4 yard cushion through the first 10 yards of the receiver's stem.
Pump the arms naturally in a tight, compact running motion to maximize backward velocity.

rows.fault_trigger: Guessing the Route. Turning the hips inside or outside prematurely before the receiver actually declares their cut, giving up an easy break on the opposite side.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Remain perfectly square and uncommitted until the exact moment the receiver physically declares their cut.
Keep body weight perfectly centered to maintain immediate multi-directional breaking ability.
Maintain strict inside alignment, physically forcing the receiver to run through your vision to cross the field.
Keep the hips low and square to establish a dominant top-down relationship.
Stay primed to explode downhill on anything thrown short, or to instantly flip and run if they push deep vertical.
Keep the shoulders strictly parallel to the line of scrimmage for the absolute maximum time possible.

rows.fault_trigger: Biting on Inside In-Breaks. Panicking and chasing a shallow inside route, leaving the deep outside completely open to a wheel or corner-route double-move.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain an outside-in trailing pocket, ensuring the receiver remains entirely inside the field of vision.
Physically and spatially force the receiver to work inward toward the safety help.

rows.fault_trigger: Reaching for the Ball Early. Turning your head to look for the deep ball before you have physically capped the receiver's shoulder, resulting in a pass interference or a separation touchdown.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Prioritize capping the receiver's outside shoulder to eliminate all deep boundary routes.
Read the receiver's exact acceleration rate and trajectory during the glide.
Enforce a strict "stay over the top" rule to guarantee you remain the deepest player on the field.

rows.fault_trigger: "Sinking the Hips Too Late". Letting a vertical receiver get within 3 yards of your cushion before you transition into a full sprint, allowing them to instantly stack you vertically.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: If the receiver reaches top speed at 8 yards, immediately transition from a backpedal into a full hip-flip run.
Keep eyes locked on the target's core frame, ready to drive downhill the absolute microsecond their hips sink for a break.

rows.fault_trigger: Bailing Deep Too Fast. Running backward immediately at the snap, which leaves the flat wide open for quick hitches or arrow routes.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take an immediate lateral shuffle or a 45-degree drop step directly toward the flat zone.
Push off the front foot directly into a tempo pedal or lateral side-shuffle (slide technique).

rows.fault_trigger: False Stepping Forward. Taking a step forward at the snap, which surrenders a piece of the high cushion before the play even develops.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Initiate a smooth read-and-drift pedal backward at a strict 45-degree angle.
Push off the forward foot and reach backward strictly with the toes of the back foot.

rows.fault_trigger: "Opening the Gate". Turning the back entirely to the sideline, allowing receivers to run easily into the deep hole behind the flat.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the chest squarely facing the quarterback throughout the drop to monitor the backfield.
Keep eyes locked on the "triangle" visual read (scanning from the nearest eligible receiver to the quarterback).
Sustain a wide, highly active base to ensure multi-directional readiness.
Force any outside release inward to physically compress the perimeter passing lane.

rows.fault_trigger: "Squatting" Early. Stopping the backward movement because of a short route underneath, which allows a deeper vertical route to fly behind you.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Match the vertical climb of the receiver exactly while executing the controlled retreat.

rows.fault_trigger: Staring at the QB. Locking eyes onto the backfield, which causes the corner to completely lose track of the receiver's intermediate crossing or out-breaking route.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish and strictly keep a depth cushion of 2 to 3 yards above the highest threat in your zone.
Keep the hips completely loose and slightly uncoiled to maintain explosive potential.
Stay primed to quickly transition into a full vertical sprint if challenged deep.

rows.fault_trigger: Turning the Hips to the Sideline Early. Turning entirely away from the field, which creates a massive visual blind spot across the inside hash marks.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain absolute depth leverage to protect the deep boundary or deep third/fourth.
Keep the upper body square to the quarterback to read the ball's trajectory upon release.
Maintain peripheral visual awareness of the receiver's vertical stem while watching the QB.
Keep the feet tracking wide and low to the turf to preserve maximum lateral break power.

rows.fault_trigger: "Reaching" / High Foot Lift. Lifting the knees high or reaching too far backward with the feet, which locks the knees and stops quick lateral redirection.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the cleats low to the grass; never lift the knees high.

rows.fault_trigger: Standing Tall. Straightening the spine, which raises the center of gravity and strips away all explosive downhill break power.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a strict forward body lean with the chest over the knees and the chin tucked.
Pump the arms in a tight, compact running motion to generate backward velocity.
Keep the chest completely square to the line of scrimmage, allowing for a read and break in any direction.

rows.fault_trigger: Over-Staggering. Setting the feet too far apart front-to-back, which traps the hips and prevents a fast lateral change of direction.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place feet strictly at shoulder-width with a tight, highly disciplined toe-to-instep stagger.

rows.fault_trigger: Bailing Deep Immediately. Turning and running deep at the snap, leaving a soft flat zone wide open for easy underneath completions.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take an immediate lateral "kick-glide" step toward your assigned zone track.
Execute a highly patient lateral weave or a controlled tempo pedal.

rows.fault_trigger: False Stepping Forward. Stepping forward at the snap, which surrenders a piece of the high cushion before the play develops.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Initiate a smooth read-and-drift backpedal at a strict 45-degree angle.
Execute a highly balanced "motor-patter" or immediate mirror step on the snap.
Load exactly 65% of body weight onto the ball of the front foot.

rows.fault_trigger: Stance Too Deep or Tall. Setting up with a high chest, which reduces lateral acceleration and makes you vulnerable to an immediate jam or a quick slant.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink the hips completely low and bend the knees deeply.
Hold hands high and loaded specifically at chin level, ready to strike.
Lock eyes squarely onto the slot receiver's beltline.
Hold your strict depth line during the lateral movement to establish a wall.
Keep the chest completely square to the line of scrimmage to read the lane.

rows.fault_trigger: Reaching with a Double-Hand Punch. Lunging forward with both hands, throwing away your balance and letting the receiver easily swipe past you.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoot a violent, independent one-handed jam directly into the receiver's shoulder frame.
Force the receiver inside or out, thoroughly disrupting their route timing.

rows.fault_trigger: Chasing Crossers Out of the Zone. Turning to chase a receiver who is leaving your zone, which creates a massive void behind you for a stunting route.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Read the triangle flow scanning from the slot threat to the quarterback.

rows.fault_trigger: Cleat-Sticking. Planting your feet heavily upon first contact, leaving you unable to match an intermediate cut or break.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the base wide and the feet low to the turf, actively sliding the cleats rather than lifting.
Establish and maintain a strict 2-yard cushion above the highest threat in your zone.
Keep the hips perfectly square to maintain a top-down frame.
Use the angled drift to fiercely protect your deep zone width.
Keep the upper body slightly forward-leaning with the chin tucked to preserve break power.
Keep the feet moving continuously; never settle into a static position.

rows.fault_trigger: Staring Down the QB. Locking eyes onto the backfield, which causes you to completely miss a vertical slot running free down your seam.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Prioritize vertical depth at all times to stay over the top of high-speed slots.

rows.fault_trigger: Rising on the Snap. Standing tall on the first step, which raises your pad level and strips away your ability to change direction quickly.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the feet completely low to the grass while moving them rapidly in place.
Keep weight perfectly centered over the core, remaining strictly neutral.

rows.fault_trigger: Guessing the Release. Lunging inside or outside before the receiver actually declares their cut, conceding an easy release on the opposite side.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold the neutral frame until the exact moment the receiver commits to a shoulder path.
The split-second the lane is chosen, slide the base laterally to frame the receiver tightly between your knees.

rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Stance. Setting the feet too close together, which restricts lateral agility and causes tripping when breaking.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Set the feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart to ensure lateral agility.

rows.fault_trigger: Bailing Hard Early. Flying backward at top speed without reading the play first, which leaves a massive void in the intermediate middle of the field.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take low, smooth "read steps" backward immediately on the snap.

rows.fault_trigger: "False Stepping Backward". Taking a step backward out of habit before running forward, which completely ruins the timing of the short-zone interception or tackle.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drive violently off the ball of the back foot the instant the read is confirmed.

rows.fault_trigger: "Squatting" Too Early. Freezing on an underneath crosser and leaving the intermediate hole wide open for a dig or a post route behind them.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a slow "pedal-patter" or an interior weave step directly off the snap.

rows.fault_trigger: Biting on Play-Action. Running downhill on a run-fake, which lets deep vertical routes (like seams or posts) stack behind you for an easy touchdown.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take exactly 3 fluid, high-depth read-steps directly backward.

rows.fault_trigger: Losing Leverage. Allowing the receiver to cleanly cross your face and establish leverage because you took a poor approach angle.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take an intentional, targeted angle-approach step out of the stance.
Implement a minimal, highly comfortable toe-to-instep stagger.

rows.fault_trigger: Static/Heavy Base. Locking the knees or resting weight heavily on the heels pre-snap, which creates a massive delay on the snap.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Distribute weight exactly 50/50 strictly on the balls of the feet.
Sink into a deep knee bend while maintaining a long, completely flat spine.
Hold the hands relaxed and highly active near the mid-torso, completely clear of the thighs.
Slide the toes across the turf without gaining excessive deep yardage initially.
Keep the chest leaning slightly forward over the toes to stay in a constant position to break downhill.

rows.fault_trigger: Clicking Heels. Letting the feet knock together during the pedal, ruining structural balance and change-of-direction speed.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain strictly parallel foot tracks during the retreat.
Keep the base wide and active while reading the quarterback's initial drop.
Take an explosive 6-to-12 inch forward step directly toward the short zone target.

rows.fault_trigger: High Pad Level. Exploding downhill with an upright chest, making the safety an easy target for blockers or causing missed tackles in the hole.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hips low and the chin strictly tucked to maintain leverage through line of scrimmage traffic.
Keep the hands up and completely punch-ready on the approach.
Prepare to aggressively clear any climbing offensive line or tight end blocks.
Use the patter step to fluidly absorb the initial depth of the route stems.
Keep eyes locked firmly strictly on the quarterback's eyes and shoulders to track passing intent.

rows.fault_trigger: Turning the Hips Early. Flipping the hips sideways, which concedes half of your zone coverage width instantly.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a neutral, square lower body posture to preserve lateral agility.
Hold the square posture until the exact moment the ball is thrown or a vertical threat physically forces a hip flip.
Use the read-steps to precisely gauge the overall vertical speed of the field.
Maintain a strict top-down visual perspective on all developing routes.

rows.fault_trigger: Drifting Unnecessarily. Drifting too far to one hash mark early without a clear threat, leaving the opposite deep seam heavily exposed.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish and strictly keep a depth cushion of 4 to 5 yards above the highest vertical threat.
Keep the feet moving in a smooth, continuous backpedal while keeping the hips completely unlocked.
Use the approach vector to strictly maintain the assigned shade (inside or outside leverage) as you close the distance.
Keep eyes locked entirely on the receiver's hip/waist cylinder to render upper-body fakes useless.
Close the spatial gap aggressively to squeeze the receiver's route.

rows.fault_trigger: Lunging at the Break. Throwing the upper body forward when the receiver makes their first cut, resulting in an easy separation and a missed tackle.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition seamlessly from the approach into a tight, trailing mirror-step the second you enter the catch zone.

rows.fault_trigger: "Linebacker Creep". Setting up with a stance that is too wide and flat, with hands resting on the thighs, which locks up the feet and causes immediate delay against a quick pass route.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place feet slightly wider than shoulder-width with an assertive toe-to-instep stagger, keeping the foot closest to the formation's core forward.

rows.fault_trigger: False Stepping Backward. Taking a step backward out of reflex, which surrenders the short-zone cushion and lets tight ends or pulling guards easily establish leverage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drive violently off the inside ball of the back foot.

rows.fault_trigger: "Squatting" Too Early. Freezing on an underneath release, leaving the intermediate space behind you wide open for a dig or a post route.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a precise lateral shuffle-weave or a slow tempo-pedal backward.

rows.fault_trigger: Biting on Play-Action. Running forward on a run-fake, letting vertical seam routes stack behind your deep cushion for an easy touchdown.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take exactly 3 fluid read-steps backward on the snap.

rows.fault_trigger: Losing the Shade. Taking an improper approach angle that allows the receiver to cross your face and establish easy leverage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take an assertive angle-approach step directly out of the stance.

rows.fault_trigger: Heel Settling. Resting weight flatly on the heels, which prevents an explosive downhill or lateral launch.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep 60% of body weight balanced directly over the ball of the front foot.
Tuck the chin over the chest and ensure the knees are aligned directly over the toes.
Hinge the hips low into a loaded, powerful position.
Hold hands loosely near the ribs, primed to instantly shed a climbing blocker or jam a receiver.
Execute a short, crisp 6-inch power step forward.

rows.fault_trigger: Lunging Tall. Flying downhill with a high chest, exposing your framework to blocks or causing slipped tackles.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the pad level strictly lower than the oncoming offensive line block or tight end frame.
Lock eyes intensely on the near-hip of the eligible receiver or primary run-key.
Gain ground aggressively downhill or laterally to squeeze the throwing window or seal the run lane.
Keep the base wide and stable throughout the movement.
Maintain parallel foot tracks; never let the feet click together or the stance narrow.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips Flipping Sideways Early. Turning entirely sideways before the route declares, giving away your coverage width.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the chest completely square to the line of scrimmage.
Read the overall flow of the passing concept while monitoring the quarterback's eyes.
Use the read-steps to precisely measure the vertical speed of the field.
Maintain a strict top-down visual perspective on the routes.

rows.fault_trigger: Drifting Prematurely. Drifting toward a hash mark too early without a clear threat, opening up a massive deep vertical void.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold a deep cushion consistently above the highest vertical threat.
Keep the hips unlocked and fluid, ready to transition from a pedal to a sprint.
Lock in your pre-snap shade leverage (inside or outside) aggressively.
Keep eyes locked entirely on the receiver's hip/waist cylinder, completely ignoring upper body fakes.

rows.fault_trigger: Lunging at the Break. Throwing your torso forward when the receiver enters the catch window, causing you to slip or miss the trail entirely.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition smoothly into a tight, trailing mirror-step once you enter the catch zone.
Keep the base wide and athletic during the trail to maintain balance.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Two-part signal reusing the established Stance-family design: (1) Stagger - horizontal distance between rear and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index), image plane, side view, torso-length scaled (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center). Coaching target: minimal/near-zero stagger. (2) Squareness - shoulder-line and hip-line horizontal-ness, front view, confirming a balanced, non-rotated base. NOTE: 'weight centered over the ball' is not measurable without ball tracking; this signal covers foot/torso geometry only, and needs both Side and Front footage to cover both sub-checks fully.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced 2-point or 3-point stance with a minimal toe-to-instep stagger over the ball, securing immediate visual alignment on the head-up or shaded nose tackle.

rows.fault_trigger: Ducking Head on Snap. Dropping the chin and breaking spine angle on the snap, losing visual tracking of the defender and surrendering leverage.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Three-part signal: (1) First-step latency - frame offset between the snap event and the first detectable ankle displacement past a small noise threshold. NOTE: this needs a ball/snap-frame reference the pose pipeline doesn't provide alone (needs ball tracking or a manually marked snap frame) - pose can detect WHEN the foot moves, not whether that lines up with the actual snap. (2) Base width retention - lateral ankle-to-ankle distance, confirming it doesn't narrow below the Phase 1 baseline. (3) Torso lean ('spine flat') - Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center angle vs. vertical, watched for a sudden drop. Knee flexion angle (Left/Right Knee) is directly measurable; 'zero drop in height' needs the pre-snap frame as a comparison baseline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap the ball crisply while simultaneously executing an immediate post step or brace step, preserving a shoulder-width base with zero drop in height.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Hip height drop from the Phase 1 baseline (Pelvis Center vertical displacement) and knee flexion angle, confirming the sink into a lower base. Shoulder-line horizontal-ness (front view) confirms square framing. NOTE: 'defender framed between the knees' is NOT measurable - there is no real defender in this simulated rep, and even with one, single-subject pose tracking doesn't register a second person's position relative to the blocker's frame. This signal covers the blocker's own base/hip/shoulder geometry only.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a wide, stable pocket wall immediately; sink the hips back into a quarter-squat, centering the imaginary nose tackle directly between both knees.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Wrist-to-sternum closing distance and elbow-to-torso tuck angle at the strike frame, confirming hands drive inside and elbows stay tight rather than flaring. NOTE: 'thumbs up' hand orientation is not measurable by body pose - that's hand-landmarker territory, not wired into this checkpoint; 'maximum kinetic force' is not directly measurable, only wrist displacement velocity as a rough proxy (would need Needs Motion tier for that specific sub-signal, not attempted here).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoot a compact, violent two-handed strike directly into the defender's chest plate with thumbs up and elbows tucked to absorb interior power.

rows.fault_trigger: "Pop and Stop". Snapping the ball, landing initial contact, and freezing foot movement, allowing the rusher to effortlessly shed the block.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Continuous small-amplitude ankle displacement across the rep window (the 'churn'), confirming the feet never stop moving for an extended run of consecutive frames. Elbow angle stability confirms 'locked arms' (staying within a narrow range rather than collapsing). NOTE: 'anchor locked' as a defensive-pressure-resisting outcome isn't measurable without an actual opposing force; this only confirms the blocker's own footwork/arm-lock mechanics continued, not whether they successfully anchored against a real rusher.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sustain continuous 6-inch choppy steps into the turf, maintaining inside hand control and keeping the defender framed between the legs until the pass is released.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Reuses the Stagger design: horizontal distance between rear/front foot ground-contact points, side view, torso-length scaled. Coaching target: minimal/near-zero stagger. Secondary signal: knee-over-ankle forward lean angle as a rough proxy for 'weight centered over the balls of the feet' - pose can't measure actual foot-pressure distribution, only the resulting body lean, so this is an approximation, not a direct measurement.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced 3-point stance with zero to minimal toe-to-instep stagger, centering weight primarily over the balls of the feet for an explosive launch.

rows.fault_trigger: "Roll-Snapping". Rolling the shoulders forward over the toes during the snap, causing the center to lunge, lose balance, and get easily pulled down by the defender.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Two-part signal: (1) First-step onset timing relative to the snap - same limitation as pass-set: needs a ball/snap-frame reference the pose pipeline doesn't provide alone. (2) Direction of travel - Pelvis Center displacement vector over the first several frames, confirming a downhill (forward) vs. lateral burst matches the called play. Torso lean ('spine flat') - Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center angle vs. horizontal, confirming a flat, driving posture rather than standing tall. NOTE: needs both Front (lateral direction) and Side (torso flatness) coverage; single-angle footage only partially confirms this checkpoint.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Initiate forward displacement while cleanly executing the snap, firing downhill to split the nose tackle (0/1-technique) or laterally to cut off the A-gap before the defender can penetrate.

rows.fault_trigger: "Gazing". Raising the eyes early to look for second-level linebackers before cleanly securing the down-lineman first.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Lateral symmetry of knee/ankle position relative to Pelvis Center's forward path - confirms the blocker's own stride stays centered and square rather than drifting to one side. NOTE: 'defender framed between the knees' is NOT measurable - there is no real defender in this simulated rep, and single-subject pose tracking wouldn't register a second person's position relative to the blocker even if there were one. This signal covers the blocker's own stride symmetry only.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the first power step directly through the crotch of the imaginary defender, framing the target tightly between both knees.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Wrist-to-sternum closing distance and elbow-to-torso tuck angle at the strike frame, confirming the punching hand drives inside with elbows tight. NOTE: this is a ONE-handed strike ('off-hand' punch), unlike Blocking-Pass Center's two-handed strike - pose alone can't determine which specific hand is the designated 'off-hand' without play-context, so track whichever wrist shows the dominant closing-distance spike. 'Maximum kinetic force' is not directly measurable, only wrist displacement velocity as a rough proxy (not attempted here).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Fire a violent, compact punch inside the chest/numbers using the off-hand immediately to establish dominant control, keeping elbows tightly tucked.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Continuous small-amplitude ankle displacement across the rep window (the 'chat steps'), confirming the feet never stop moving for an extended run of consecutive frames - reuses the churn signal from Blocking-Pass Center's Finish phase. Forward Pelvis Center displacement over the same window confirms sustained forward drive (the Matrix's 'vertical displacement' means downfield drive here, not literal vertical movement).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition instantly from the initial power step into short, rapid 6-inch "chat steps" to drive the defender vertically.

rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Base. Setting your feet at a standard shoulder-width. A narrow base during a shotgun snap destroys your balance, causing you to tip forward the moment you snap the ball.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Approach the line and straddle the midline of the ball, spreading your feet 4 inches wider than shoulder-width to build an unyielding, broad anchor. Keep your spine flat, your chest proud, and your belt line perfectly square to the line of scrimmage, remaining completely balanced.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling. Coaching target: feet should show no consistent vertical offset (0-inch stagger). NOTE: absolute-inch conversion needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture - open decision, not yet built); until then this reports a relative torso-length value only, uncalibrated.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a 0-inch stagger — a perfectly parallel base — with neither foot ahead of the other.

rows.fault_trigger: Fingertip Leaning. Placing forward pressure onto the ball. Leaning forward causes the ball to sail high or skip off the grass, leading to critical turnover fumbles.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink your hips deeply and shift your weight heavily backward onto your heels, balancing your weight at 40% forward / 60% backward. Your cleats must stay flat and glued to the turf so you do not fall forward while snapping.

Reach your dominant hand forward to grip the center of the ball. Extend your non-dominant hand forward, resting the forearm comfortably across your non-snap thigh to build a rigid upper structural frame.

rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Base. Setting your feet at a standard shoulder-width. A narrow base during a shotgun snap destroys your balance, causing you to tip forward the moment you snap the ball.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Approach the line and straddle the midline of the ball, spreading your feet 4 inches wider than shoulder-width to build an unyielding, broad anchor. Keep your spine flat, your chest proud, and your belt line perfectly square to the line of scrimmage, remaining completely balanced.

Align with a square base, identifying the "triangle" (Nose tackle to the linebackers) to establish dual-threat awareness.

rows.fault_trigger: Getting Caught in "No Man's Land". Staring at one specific defender while a blitzer slips through the vacated adjacent gap destroys the integrity of the half-slide protection. You must protect the zone, not chase the man.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and take a diagonal 45-degree placeholder step toward the slide side.
Keep eyes actively scanning the triangle to diagnose blitzing linebackers or interior line stunts.
If a threat enters the slide gap, engage immediately; if no immediate threat appears, proactively punch and assist the guard on the man-protection side.
Maintain the hinge block or double-team structure, ensuring the interior pocket remains deep and clean.
Identify the assigned 0-technique, 1-technique, or blitzing linebacker to lock head-to-head.

rows.fault_trigger: Lunging Forward. Firing out of your stance and leaning forward allows the defender to easily use a swim or club move to bypass you instantly.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and execute a quick, vertical "Post Set" taking 1-to-2 short steps backward.
Establish a firm, immovable base by keeping the head back and the hips sunk low.
Deliver a violent, two-handed strike directly into the numbers of the interior defender.
Halt the defender's upward momentum completely and maintain the block until the pass is released.
Establish a square, parallel base under center, sinking the hips to prepare for the snap.

rows.fault_trigger: Over-Stepping Laterally. Taking a brace step wider than 6 inches creates a massive gap between you and the backside Guard, or causes your hips to turn sideways, ruining your anchor.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Immediately upon the snap, take a short, 6-inch lateral "brace step" with the foot closest to the slide direction.
Punch violently with the inside hand to intercept and control the designated A-gap.
Anchor the backside foot firmly into the turf to absorb sudden interior blitzes.
Maintain square leverage to ensure no defender crosses your face or compromises the slide line.
Identify the primary defensive lineman to double-team and locate the target second-level linebacker.

rows.fault_trigger: Climbing Too Quickly. Abandoning the double-team to climb to the second level too early leaves the defensive lineman un-secured, allowing them to split the block and instantly disrupt the backfield.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and take a hard, 45-degree "gallop step" directly into the hip of the defensive lineman.
Lock your inside shoulder tightly against the adjacent guard's outside shoulder to eliminate any physical gaps.
Keep your eyes up and focused forward to track the assigned linebacker's path while driving the defensive lineman.
Detach and peel off to the linebacker only when their jersey numbers cross your field of vision, delivering a decisive block at the second level.
Establish a balanced, coiled stance with eyes locked on the assigned interior defender.

rows.fault_trigger: Stepping Narrow or High. Coming out of the stance with a narrow base or popping completely upright surrenders all leverage, resulting in you being violently pushed backward directly into the Quarterback's or running back's path.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and fire out instantly with a low, explosive "power step" right through the crotch (midline) of the defender.
Follow the initial strike instantly with a short "chat step" to establish a wide, anchored driving base.
Shoot the hands violently inside the defender's frame to gain inside leverage and chest control.
Maintain low leverage and drive the legs continuously using short, powerful movements to displace the defender vertically.
Identify the pull direction, the intended insertion gap, and the target linebacker assignment.

rows.fault_trigger: Turning the Hips and Running. Turning your hips and running like a sprinter blocks your vision of the second-level flow, makes it impossible to adjust to a linebacker's counter-movement, and leaves the backside open.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap, push aggressively off the play-side foot, and take a lateral step backward with the backside foot to clear the line.
"Skip" laterally behind the line of scrimmage while keeping the shoulders parallel to the end zone to maintain full vision of the defense.
Plant the outside foot and violently transition from lateral movement to a vertical sprint, inserting into the designated gap.
Engage the target linebacker the exact moment they commit, driving upward to clear the running lane.
Identify the penetrating defender designated to be trapped and mentally lock onto the nearest inside threat to down-block.

rows.fault_trigger: Slowing the Timing. Allowing the purposefully bypassed defender to touch, chip, or slow you down in any way. You must clear the space instantly to allow your pulling teammate an unobstructed path to deliver the trap block.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap and take a sharp, heavy "down block" step at an inside angle directly away from the trapped defender.
Clear the path completely cleanly; do not make eye contact, attempt to chip, or engage with the defender being trapped.
Immediately seek out the next nearest interior defensive lineman or flowing linebacker down the line of scrimmage.
Engage the secondary threat with maximum force, pinning them inside to create a clean wall for the pulling player and ball carrier.

Approach the ball and straddle the midline of the football, spacing your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart to create a highly stable, square anchor. Keep your belt line completely square to the line of scrimmage. Ensure your head is up, neck is relaxed, and chest is proud to comfortably see the defensive front and call out protections.

rows.fault_trigger: Unconscious Stagger. Allowing one foot to drift backward out of a habit. Any stagger from the Center creates an offset gap under your hips, causing quarterback-center exchange fumbles.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Vertical (image-Y) position of each foot's ground-contact point (Heel/Foot Index) relative to the other, scaled by hip height as the reference for foreshortening. The foot appearing higher in frame (smaller image-Y) is the one staggered further back from the camera - an ordinary perspective artifact of a level, front-facing camera, not a depth estimate (no MediaPipe Z used). Gives ORDER (which foot is back) and a rough relative magnitude only, not a precise inch value - front view cannot resolve depth-axis distance precisely. Coaching target: feet should show no consistent vertical offset (0-inch stagger). NOTE: this is a deliberately weaker signal than the side-view version of this same checkpoint; use side view whenever available.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Approach the ball and straddle the midline of the football. Set your feet completely parallel (0-inch stagger / perfectly square), spaced slightly wider than shoulder-width apart to create a highly stable, square anchor.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Set your feet completely parallel — a 0-inch stagger, perfectly square — with neither foot ahead of the other.

rows.fault_trigger: Leaning on the Ball. Placing too much upper-body weight directly onto the football. If the ball slips, you will collapse instantly into the dirt.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink your hips straight down into a deep squat, keeping your weight distributed evenly on the balls of both feet (50/50 balance). Do not lean heavily forward onto the ball, as this ruins your ability to handle a sudden defensive nose-guard rush.

Reach your dominant hand forward to grip the football cleanly along the laces. Extend your non-dominant arm forward, resting your elbow or forearm lightly on your non-snap thigh to lock in a rigid, structural framework.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso lean angle: the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line angle relative to vertical, tracked from Stance Locking into Coiled Readiness. rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold your position firmly as the quarterback rides directly under your hips. Keep your back completely flat and your ankles, knees, and hips flexed like a tightly compressed coil, ready to deliver a clean snap and immediately strike the defender.
Squeeze the distance down strictly to 1-2 yards from the defender before executing the launch.

rows.fault_trigger: "Telegraphing the Cut". Lowering the pad level too early or staring at the defender's shins before launching, alerting them to brace or swim.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Aim your front shoulder directly at the thigh pad or knee line of the oncoming defender.

rows.fault_trigger: "Diving at the Ankles". Throwing the body too low or too early, allowing the defender to easily step over the block or swat the back down without breaking stride.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Launch horizontally across the defender's frame, physically throwing your body sideways.

rows.fault_trigger: Leading with the Head. Launching head-first into a defender's knees, creating a dangerous risk for neck and concussive injuries.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ensure the back or side of your shoulder connects with their legs to force the takedown.
Keep the head up and eyes locked entirely on the target through the entirety of the strike to protect the neck.
Align in a comfortable stance with the left foot staggered back to set efficiently to the left B-gap or A-gap threat.

rows.fault_trigger: Opening the Gate. Bailing out too wide with the left foot and turning hips outward, opening a massive A-gap lane.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a short, crisp angle set to the left, taking weight onto the inside leg (70/30 distribution) while keeping the base wide.
Keep the hips low and square, framing the incoming rusher directly between the legs to shut down counter moves.
Deliver an independent outside-pillar punch with the left hand into the defender's shoulder/chest, followed by the right hand under the chest plate.

rows.fault_trigger: "Sticking the Cleats". Planting the feet heavy upon first contact, leaving the guard vulnerable to a quick arm-over or spin move.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shuffle laterally in low, active short steps, constantly resetting the base to mirror the defender until pass release.

rows.fault_trigger: "Telegraphing". Placing too much weight heavily onto the down hand for a drive block, or leaning back on the heels when preparing to pull, tipping off the defense.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Assume a powerful 3-point stance with a slight left-foot-back stagger (toe-to-instep) to anchor and push forward-diagonal paths.
Trigger an aggressive, forward angle of departure to act as an interior engine to physically displace defensive tackles and secure the inside gap.

rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Base. Stepping too narrow on the second step, allowing the defender to easily push the guard sideways.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drive the feet wide apart on parallel tracks so the imaginary defender's core remains strictly framed between the guard's thighs.
Shoot both hands straight out from the dirt into the inside V of the chest plate, exploding up through the palms with thumbs up to lift the opponent.
Run the feet relentlessly on contact, keeping cleats low to the ground and continuously pumping forward to finish the block.

rows.fault_trigger: Pre-Angling Hips. Turning your lower body outward toward the perimeter before the snap. This tips off the defense to an outside zone run or a slide protection schema.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take a wide 12-to-18-inch split from the Center, placing your right foot forward. Keep your spine straight, your chest upright, and your shoulders squared completely to the defensive line.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stagger your left foot back exactly 3 to 4 inches, locking your left toe into a direct line with the mid-foot arch of your right shoe.
Drop your weight low and backward, locking in a 45% forward / 55% backward split, keeping the bulk of your power stored in your heels and core.
Drop your left hand to the turf into a light 3-point contact stance, using your fingertips solely for balance. Rest your right hand securely on your right thigh.

rows.fault_trigger: High Hips. Standing up too vertical in a 3-point stance. High hips strip away your lower-body power, allowing defenders to easily push you into the quarterback's face.

rows.fault_trigger: Dropping Too Deep. Dropping too deep backward in the pass set abandons the line of scrimmage. This forces the pocket to shrink vertically, allowing the defensive line to easily compress the space around the quarterback and disrupt the throw.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, set at a controlled 45-degree angle to the left, keeping a perfectly balanced weight distribution on the balls of the feet.
Keep an inside hand extended to "feel" for a stunting interior lineman while keeping your eyes locked on the edge threat.
Depending on the stunt development, be ready to seamlessly pass off the interior defender or catch the looping rusher coming from the outside.
Secure the designated target and drop the anchor, ensuring the depth of the pocket remains entirely intact.
Identify the specific interior assignment (typically a 3-technique defensive tackle) and lock in a balanced pass-blocking stance.

rows.fault_trigger: Bending at the Waist. Reaching forward and bending at the waist completely shifts your weight off your anchor. This makes you highly susceptible to "push-pull" or "swim" moves, allowing the defender to effortlessly throw you face-first into the turf.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap count and execute an aggressive "Angle Set" (a quick 45-degree lateral-forward step to the left) to instantly close the distance to the defender.
Keep the spine completely straight and the chest up as you approach contact, refusing to lean forward.
Keep the hands loaded tight to the torso, then deliver a violent, independent hand punch to disrupt the defender's rush path.
Lock out the arms, sink the hips, and continuously mirror the defender to deny any inside or outside counter moves.
Identify the slide direction and mentally lock down the designated gap responsibility (A-gap or B-gap).

rows.fault_trigger: Chasing the Looper. Chasing a defensive lineman who purposefully loops outside completely vacates your assigned zone. This opens up an easy, direct interior lane for an inside stunting lineman to hit the Quarterback untouched.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a lateral "catch step" to the left directly into the designated slide gap space.
Keep the upper body perfectly square to the line of scrimmage with hands extended, ready to absorb contact.
Protect the physical gap space itself. Wait for the threat to come to you; do not abandon the zone to chase a looping defender.
Maintain the structural integrity of the interior wall, ensuring no stunting lineman can exploit the interior lane.
Identify your blocking partner (either the Center or Left Tackle) and target the designated interior defensive lineman, noting the second-level linebacker's alignment.

rows.fault_trigger: Splitting Apart. Stepping too shallow or failing to merge hip-to-hip leaves a physical seam between you and your blocking partner. This allows an aggressive, heavy defensive end to split the double team, breach the wall, and blow up the play in the backfield.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a heavy lateral power step directly toward your teammate to instantly close any physical space between you.
Merge entirely hip-to-hip with your blocking partner. Glue your inside hand securely to your partner's hip or lower back to ensure physical unity.
Drive horizontally off the line of scrimmage as a combined unit. Keep your head up and your outside hand completely free to strike the approaching linebacker.
Once the defensive tackle is rolled backward or secured by your partner, seamlessly detach and absorb the second-level linebacker.
Identify the isolated interior defender and establish a heavily coiled run-blocking stance.

rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Bring the Hips Through. Hitting the defender without rolling your hips through the contact results in a weak, top-heavy block. Relying entirely on upper-body strength guarantees you will lose leverage and get shed.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, explode forward out of the stance with a powerful displacement step to instantly close the cushion.
Shoot the hands violently upward and directly into the defender's armpits to gain inside control.
Sink the hips heavily upon initial contact, then immediately lift upward to completely break the defender's leverage.
Keep the feet wide and unceasingly active ("run your feet") to generate continuous vertical movement down the field.
Identify the designated pull direction (to the right), the intended insertion hole, and the target linebacker assignment.

rows.fault_trigger: Crossing the Feet. Crossing the trailing foot over the lead foot during the skip completely destroys your base. It guarantees you will trip over your own feet or immediately lose your balance and get knocked over upon hitting a defender.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, open immediately with a short lateral slide step to the right.
Bring the trailing left foot along without crossing it over the lead foot. Keep the chest completely facing the line of scrimmage to maintain vision.
Keep your eyes up-field, locate the target linebacker, and violently burst forward into the designated hole.
Make decisive contact with the second-level defender, driving your momentum entirely through their frame to clear the lane.
Identify the designated pull path and mentally lock onto the unblocked edge or interior defender slated for the kick-out.

rows.fault_trigger: Pulling Too Deep. Looping backward into the backfield instead of running a tight line allows the unblocked defender to penetrate too deeply. This ruins the geometry of the play and results in a tackle for loss.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take an aggressive, perfectly flat "open step" to the right, pivoting exactly 90 degrees on the right foot.
Run a tight, straight line right across the heels of the remaining offensive linemen; do not bow or loop backward into the backfield.
As you close the distance on the penetrating defender, intentionally drop your inside shoulder to establish lower leverage.
Deliver a violent, explosive kick-out block directly into the defender's flank, completely clearing them out of the running lane.

rows.fault_trigger: Turning Inward. Allowing your left hip and shoulder to angle toward the Center. This restricts your ability to pass-block an exterior rusher attacking your outside gap.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align with a tight split next to the Center, setting your right foot forward. Keep your chest and shoulders squared completely to the defensive front line, preventing any pre-snap physical tipping of your assignment.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align with a tight split next to the Center. Set your right foot forward and stagger your left foot back exactly 4 to 6 inches, so your left toe aligns directly with the mid-foot or instep of your right shoe.

Lower your hips and keep your balance at roughly 60% forward / 40% backward to prioritize an aggressive under-center run launch. Keep the balls of your feet dug firmly into the grass.
Drop your left hand cleanly to the turf into a 3-point stance, resting light fingertip pressure on the ground. Tuck your right arm close to your right thigh to complete your upper structural frame.

rows.fault_trigger: Squatting Too High. Leaving your hips too high before the snap. Standing too upright strips away your natural leverage.

Align in an unweighted 2-point stance, left foot staggered back, hands held loosely at mid-chest, weight on balls of feet.
Push off the inside right leg (70/30 weight distribution) into a deep 45-degree or vertical kick slide with the left foot.
Keep base wide and hips sunk in a quarter-squat, ensuring the rusher's path remains centered relative to your core frame between the legs.

rows.fault_trigger: Reaching / Clapping. Extending both hands prematurely with wide elbows, stripping away length and balance.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Deliver a stiff, independent left-hand strike to the chest plate to disrupt speed, keeping the right hand locked to catch inside counter moves.

rows.fault_trigger: "Catching" the Rusher. Freezing feet while waiting for contact, destroying leverage and inviting a severe bull-rush.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain continuous foot movement, sliding laterally or vertically to stay positioned strictly between the quarterback and the rusher.
Align in a 3-point stance with left hand down, left foot staggered back (toe-to-instep), minimal weight on fingers.

rows.fault_trigger: False Stepping. Picking up the front foot and dropping it in place pre-snap, stalling the initial kick step and forcing the tackle to chase from behind.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pop cleanly out of the stance, driving off the inside right foot into an explosive 45-degree vertical kick step with the left foot.

rows.fault_trigger: Standing Up Straight. Popping upright out of the stance, raising pad level and erasing lateral redirection capabilities.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Slide the inside foot along the turf to preserve a shoulder-width-plus base, keeping the rusher centered over the outside knee.
Shoot an independent left hand punch to the defender's outside chest/shoulder, using the right hand to catch inside counters.
Continuously slide and mirror the defender's path all the way past the pocket depth, keeping feet active until the play whistles dead.
Assume a balanced 2-point upright stance with hands held loosely near the knees or chest. Left foot staggered back, completely unweighted.

rows.fault_trigger: Passive Steps. Taking a tentative, soft first step instead of an aggressive, ground-gaining lateral or drop step.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Utilize the uninhibited view of the edge to quickly read and execute wide-zone or reach blocks to seal the perimeter.

rows.fault_trigger: "Catching". Standing straight up and waiting for the defensive end to make contact, giving away all leverage advantages.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lower hips into an athletic quarter-squat on the first step. Maintain a square core to the imaginary defender so they stay centered between your legs as you run them horizontally.
Shoot the hands quickly from chest level into the inside frame of the defender, locking out the inside hand to secure leverage.
Accelerate the feet continuously through the block. Do not plant; run the defender laterally toward the sideline to clear the cutback lane.
Align in a 3-point stance with the left hand down, left foot staggered back (toe-to-heel), shifting weight forward into the fingers to trigger an instant launch.

rows.fault_trigger: "False Stepping". Picking up the front foot and dropping it in place before advancing, which ruins the timing of the play and lets the defender strike first.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Exert maximum forward power to execute a devastating down block on an interior tackle or a base block to clear the edge.

rows.fault_trigger: Over-Reaching. Lunging wildly on a reach block, causing the tackle to lose balance and drop to their knees.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hips square to the imaginary defender even when stepping at an angle, capturing and framing them perfectly between the knees.
Shoot the hands violently straight up into the armpits and inside chest, avoiding clapping out wide.
Keep the cleats moving forward in a powerful rhythm, connecting the hips directly to the defender's hips.
Set a wide 2.5-foot split from the Left Guard, placing your right foot forward. Keep your torso upright, your chest proud, and your spine completely straight and square to the line of scrimmage.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling. Coaching target: left foot staggered back the deepest amount in the set (14-16in). rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stagger your left foot back aggressively exactly 14 to 16 inches, positioning your left toe completely clear of and behind your right heel to anchor your perimeter wall.
Sink your hips and balance your weight evenly at 40% forward / 60% backward on the balls of your feet, maximizing your multi-directional agility.

rows.fault_trigger: Flaring Elbows. Letting your elbows flare out wide to the sides. Flared elbows open up your chest, allowing a defender to easily land an inside punch and control your frame.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep your hands up and open at chest level (ready to punch), or rest them lightly on your thighs with your elbows tucked securely into your ribs.

rows.fault_trigger: Lazy Core. Failing to brace your abdominal muscles before the snap. A loose core causes your lower back to buckle the moment a physical defender makes contact.

A stable angle is expected; a sudden late increase suggests the back arching/rounding as weight settles. NOTE: measures overall torso LEAN, not spinal curvature - no mid-back landmark exists in the 33-point model, so true rounding is not directly visible. Flagged Partial for that reason, not Yes.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold your loaded, half-squat posture. Keep your core fully locked and your knees bent, ready to instantly strike an inside rusher or slide out wide to protect the edge.

Identify the dual-threat defensive front (e.g., a defensive end and an outside linebacker), noting both the B-gap responsibility and the edge threat.

rows.fault_trigger: Chasing the Decoy. Aggressively kick-sliding outward to chase a defensive end who is purposely rushing wide to act as a decoy. This completely vacates the B-gap, leaving a massive, unblockable lane for a stunting linebacker to shoot through and violently hit the quarterback from the blindside.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a controlled pass set backward and slightly outward, keeping the weight heavily distributed on the inside insteps to allow for instant redirection.
Keep the inside arm engaged or extended to "feel" for a defensive end crashing the B-gap, while locking your eyes on the looping edge threat.
As the stunt develops, seamlessly pass off the crashing inside defender to the Left Guard and firmly redirect your momentum outward to intercept the looping edge rusher.
Secure the new target, drop the hips to anchor, and steer the defender safely past the depth of the quarterback's drop.
Identify the specific edge rusher (often a wide 5-technique or 9-technique) and lock in a staggered, coiled pass-blocking stance.

rows.fault_trigger: Over-Setting (Opening the Gate). Kicking backward too deeply and turning your shoulders entirely toward the sideline too early. This "opens the gate," handing the elite edge rusher a direct, unimpeded path to execute an inside counter move (like a spin or rip) straight into the Quarterback's lap.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, execute an explosive backward "kick step" with the outside (left) foot to instantly gain depth and widen the pocket.
Maintain a completely straight spine with the chest up, dragging the inside (right) foot smoothly to protect the critical inside lane.
Wait for the rusher to enter the physical strike zone, then deliver a violent, independent hand punch to halt their forward momentum.
Lock out the arms, sink the hips, and continuously kick-slide to mirror the defender, steering them harmlessly wide and past the depth of the pocket.
Identify the slide direction and mentally lock down the designated gap responsibility on the left side of the formation.

rows.fault_trigger: Chasing the Ghost. Drifting outside of your designated zone to chase a wide-rushing defensive end. In a slide protection, this entirely defeats the purpose of the scheme, tearing open a massive B-gap lane for an interior stunting tackle to hit the Quarterback immediately.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a lateral "catch step" into the designated slide gap space to immediately seal the lane.
Keep the upper body perfectly square to the line of scrimmage with hands extended, ready to absorb any threat entering your cylinder.
Protect the physical gap space itself. Wait for the threat to come to you; do not abandon the zone to chase a defender intentionally rushing excessively wide or looping away.
Maintain the structural integrity of the offensive line's perimeter, ensuring no stunting lineman can exploit the seam between you and the Left Guard.
Identify your blocking partner (Left Guard or Tight End) and target the designated defensive lineman, noting the second-level linebacker's alignment.

rows.fault_trigger: Splitting Apart. Stepping too shallow or failing to merge hip-to-hip leaves a physical seam between you and your blocking partner. This allows an aggressive, heavy defensive end to split the double team, breach the wall, and blow up the play in the backfield.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take a heavy lateral power step directly toward your teammate to instantly close any physical space between you.
Merge entirely hip-to-hip with your blocking partner. Glue your inside hand securely to your partner's hip or lower back to ensure physical unity.
Drive horizontally off the line of scrimmage as a combined unit. Keep your head up and your outside hand completely free to strike the approaching linebacker.
Once the defensive lineman is rolled backward or secured by your partner, seamlessly detach and absorb the second-level linebacker.
Identify the isolated edge defender and establish a heavily coiled, balanced run-blocking stance.

rows.fault_trigger: Lunging / Leaving the Feet Behind. Attempting to strike the defender by lunging aggressively with the upper body while the feet stop moving. This destroys your base, makes you extremely top-heavy, and allows a savvy edge defender to effortlessly pull you forward and throw you to the turf (the "pull-swim" or "judo" shed).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, explode forward out of the stance with a powerful displacement step (often a lead or base step) to instantly erase the cushion between you and the defender.
Shoot the hands violently upward and directly into the defender's breastplate or armpits to establish dominant inside control.
Sink the hips heavily upon initial contact, then immediately drive upward and forward through the hips to completely break the defender's leverage.
Keep the feet wide and unceasingly active ("run your feet") to generate continuous displacement, steering the defender away from the ball carrier's path.
Identify the designated pull direction (typically right), the intended insertion point (the hole opened by the front-side blockers), and the target linebacker assignment.

rows.fault_trigger: Drifting Too Deep (Bowing). Taking too deep of a drop step and bowing backward into the backfield during the pull. This wastes critical milliseconds, ruins the geometry of the blocking scheme, and often leads to an immediate collision with the Quarterback or Running Back.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, open immediately with a short, controlled lateral slide step to the right, ensuring you clear the depth of the guards and center.
Bring the trailing left foot along without crossing it over the lead foot. Keep the chest completely facing the line of scrimmage to scan for run-throughs and track your target.
Keep your eyes up-field, locate the target second-level defender, plant the outside foot, and violently burst forward into the designated hole.
Make decisive contact with the linebacker, establishing inside hand placement and driving your momentum entirely through their frame to clear the lane for the ball carrier.
Identify the designated pull path across the formation and mentally lock onto the unblocked interior or edge defender slated for the kick-out.

rows.fault_trigger: Pulling Too Deep. Looping backward into the backfield instead of running a tight line across the center's heels. A deep, looping path delays your arrival, allowing the unblocked defender to penetrate the backfield and blow up the play for a loss before you can execute the kick-out.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, take an aggressive, perfectly flat "open step" to the right, pivoting exactly 90 degrees on the right foot to initiate the pull.
Run a tight, straight line right across the heels of the guards and center; do not bow or loop backward into the backfield.
As you close the distance on the penetrating defender, intentionally drop your inside shoulder to establish lower leverage.
Deliver a violent, explosive kick-out block directly into the defender's flank, completely clearing them out of the running lane.
Set a wide split from the Left Guard, placing your right foot forward. Keep your torso upright, your chest proud, and your spine completely straight and square to the line of scrimmage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Aim your front shoulder directly at the thigh pad or knee line of the oncoming defender.

rows.fault_trigger: "Diving at the Ankles". Throwing the body too low or too early, allowing the defender to easily step over the block or swat the back down without breaking stride.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Launch horizontally across the defender's frame, physically throwing your body sideways.

rows.fault_trigger: Leading with the Head. Launching head-first into a defender's knees, creating a dangerous risk for neck and concussive injuries.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ensure the back or side of your shoulder connects with their legs to force the takedown.
Keep the head up and eyes locked entirely on the target through the entirety of the strike to protect the neck.
Assume a balanced stance with the right foot staggered back slightly to allow an explosive forward-diagonal angle set to the right.
Fire the right foot diagonally on an aggressive angle set to close space on a 3-technique tackle, keeping the base strictly wide.
Drag the left foot to replace the base without narrowing, keeping the defender centered between the knees and shoulders square.

rows.fault_trigger: Flaring Elbows. Allowing elbows to swing outward, exposing the guard's own chest plate to easy control.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Explode the right hand out first as the primary strike into the chest, anchoring the left hand inside the opposite pectoral to stun momentum.

rows.fault_trigger: Lunging & Over-Extending. Shifting weight onto the toes, which locks the knees, stops foot movement, and lets the rusher easily pull the guard forward.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the feet pattering in micro-steps backward to absorb any power transition, anchoring the front-side pocket wall.
Adopt a rigid, loaded 3-point stance with the right foot staggered back. Weight is balanced 60% forward and 40% back to optimize forward launch.
Explode forward to execute heavy base blocks to drive 3-techniques outward or down blocks to collapse the line.

rows.fault_trigger: Waist Bending. Bending over at the waist instead of hinging at the knees and hips, killing all leg-drive leverage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Deliver high-knee, powerful driving steps, keeping your midsection directly aligned with the center mass of the imaginary threat.

rows.fault_trigger: Elbow Flaring. Letting the elbows flare out on contact, which diminishes power and allows the defensive tackle to slide right off the block.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Explode both hands into the inside chest frame/armpits, clamping down on jersey cloth while keeping elbows tightly squeezed against the ribs.
Maintain a rapid, continuous foot-patter, keeping the drive forward with short, choppy bursts until the whistle blows.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, set at a controlled 45-degree angle to the right, keeping a perfectly balanced weight distribution on the balls of the feet.
Keep an inside hand extended to "feel" for a stunting interior lineman while keeping your eyes locked on the edge threat.
Depending on the stunt development, be ready to seamlessly pass off the interior defender or catch the looping rusher coming from the outside.
Secure the designated target and drop the anchor, ensuring the depth of the pocket remains entirely intact.
Identify the specific interior assignment (typically a 3-technique defensive tackle) and lock in a balanced pass-blocking stance.

rows.fault_trigger: Bending at the Waist. Reaching forward and bending at the waist completely shifts your weight off your anchor. This makes you highly susceptible to "push-pull" or "swim" moves, allowing the defender to effortlessly throw you face-first into the turf.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap count and execute an aggressive "Angle Set" (a quick 45-degree lateral-forward step to the right) to instantly close the distance to the defender.

Coaching target: right foot staggered back a large, clearly visible amount (10-12in). NOTE: deliberately weaker than the side-view version of this checkpoint; use side view whenever available.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take a wider 1.5-to-2-foot split from the Right Guard. Place your left foot forward and stagger your right foot back deeply exactly 10 to 12 inches, ensuring your right toe aligns directly behind your left heel to protect your outside edge.

rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Base or Weak Stagger. Setting the stagger at only 4 inches. A shallow tackle stagger allows speed-rushers to instantly clip your outside shoulder before you can get depth in a kick-slide.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling. Coaching target: 10-12 inches. NOTE: absolute-inch conversion needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture - open decision, not yet built); until then this reports a relative torso-length value only, uncalibrated.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stagger your right foot back deeply exactly 10 to 12 inches, ensuring your right toe aligns directly behind your left heel to protect your outside edge.
Drop your weight low. Keep your balance split at 55% forward / 45% backward, ensuring you have enough forward tilt to drive block an exterior edge rusher while maintaining back-foot leverage.

rows.fault_trigger: Locked Front Knee. Failing to bend your front knee sufficiently when reaching down. This forces your back to hunch and locks up your legs.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lower your right hand to the ground, placing it slightly outside your right knee frame. Keep your left hand braced securely against your left thigh to establish a rigid 3-point platform.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso lean angle: the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line angle relative to vertical, tracked from Stance Locking into Coiled Readiness. A stable angle is expected; a sudden late increase suggests the back arching/rounding as weight settles. NOTE: measures overall torso LEAN, not spinal curvature - no mid-back landmark exists in the 33-point model, so true rounding is not directly visible. Flagged Partial for that reason, not Yes.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lock your spine flat and look up. Keep your core heavily braced and your lower joints compressed like a high-tension spring, ready to launch forward or kick-slide wide.
Squeeze the distance down strictly to 1-2 yards from the defender before executing the launch.

rows.fault_trigger: "Telegraphing the Cut". Lowering the pad level too early or staring at the defender's shins before launching, alerting them to brace or swim.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Aim your front shoulder directly at the thigh pad or knee line of the oncoming defender.

rows.fault_trigger: "Diving at the Ankles". Throwing the body too low or too early, allowing the defender to easily step over the block or swat the back down without breaking stride.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Launch horizontally across the defender's frame, physically throwing your body sideways.

rows.fault_trigger: Leading with the Head. Launching head-first into a defender's knees, creating a dangerous risk for neck and concussive injuries.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ensure the back or side of your shoulder connects with their legs to force the takedown.
Keep the head up and eyes locked entirely on the target through the entirety of the strike to protect the neck.

rows.fault_trigger: "The Double-Clutch". Attempting to make a dynamic football move or break up-field before the ball is completely secured in the hands, leading to direct drops or immediate bobble-fumbles upon first contact.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Instantly secure the ball out of the snap exchange or handoff fake and transition it directly to the body, completely avoiding any "double-clutch" or premature up-field break before the ball is fully possessed.

rows.fault_trigger: "Flagging" the Ball. Carrying the ball loosely away from the body while running in space. This heavily exposes the ball to trailing defenders punching or stripping it from behind.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hook the fingers over the front point, press the forearm along the seam, and clamp the back half of the football securely between the forearm and bicep.

rows.fault_trigger: Exposing the Breast. Carrying the football across the middle of the chest with a nose-up orientation. This allows a defender to punch it cleanly and violently out from the front.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Press the inner side of the football firmly against the rib cage with the nose tucked up beneath the armpit, completely locking the elbow to the torso to eliminate daylight.
Read interior pursuit and transfer the ball to the outside arm (closest to the sideline), freeing the inside arm to stiff-arm or guard against incoming tacklers.
The moment traffic closes in or a tackle is initiated, wrap the off-hand over the ball (two-handed carry) and chin the football to protect it completely through the ground.

rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding or extra movement disrupting the quick base.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet efficient + under the body — stable base without excessive stride length or unnecessary movement. Foot placement measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the feet efficiently under the body — the step creating a stable base without excessive stride length or unnecessary movement.

rows.fault_trigger: Indecisive first step or drifting off the throwing platform.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Decisive first step in the designed direction while maintaining balance + preparing the throwing platform — create rhythm without drifting. First-step measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a decisive first step in the designed direction while maintaining balance and preparing the throwing platform — creating proper throwing rhythm without drifting.

rows.fault_trigger: Out of sync with the quick-game timing.
